claims.claim: Perfume concentrations range from 2-5% for Eau de Cologne up to 15-25% for Extrait, with the remainder being ethanol solvent.
claims.episode_span: The concentrate itself is a blend of natural essential oils and synthetic aroma chemicals, typically making up between two and twenty-five percent of the finished liquid depending on the intended strength.
claims.supporting_quote: Concentrations vary from 3% – 25% of perfume oil and the higher the ratio of oil the more intense and long lasting the perfume will be.

claims.claim: Ethyl alcohol serves as the neutral, odorless solvent that dissolves fragrance concentrate in alcoholic perfumes, typically comprising 70-92% of the formula.
claims.episode_span: Ethanol serves as the solvent because it dissolves the hydrophobic aromatic molecules, evaporates quickly on skin, and leaves the scent behind without residue.
claims.source_title: Alcohol and perfume: denatured alcohol, alcohol-free & concentration — Carrément Belle (research)
claims.supporting_quote: An alcoholic fragrance is between 70% and 92% alcohol, depending on the type of fragrance chosen (eau de Cologne, eau de toilette, eau de parfum, perfume…).
